newsitem.title: FRANCE: Jospin to attend Franco-German summit June 13.
newsitem.headline: Jospin to attend Franco-German summit June 13.

text.p: French Prime Minister Lionel Jospin said on Thursday he planned to attend a Franco-German summit in Poitiers, western France, on June 13.

He will accompany French President Jacques Chirac in what will be the first time both attend an international meeting together since a parliamentary election on Sunday swept Jospin's Socialist party to power.
The regular Franco-German summits are usually attended by heads of state, the French prime minister, finance and foreign ministers and other ministers of both governments.
Asked whether he would attend the summit, Jospin replied, "Yes, naturally. It's the rule."
Jospin, who afterwards left Paris to fly to Malmo, Sweden, where he was to address a gathering of Socialist heads of governments and parties.
He said he would speak to German Chancellor Helmut Kohl by telephone when he returned on Friday.
He said he called Kohl on Tuesday but could not reach him and the chancellor left on a foreign trip afterwords.
"We have arranged to speak by telephone when I return from Malmo," Jospin said.
